title: Nihon Bridge: Morning Scene (Nihonbashi, asa no kei)
note: A daimyo procession sets off across Nihonbashi at dawn as fish vendors and porters crowd the bridgehead, marking the start of the Tōkaidō in Edo.
look: Fish vendors and porters crowd the bridgehead as the procession sets out, and the city is still in dawn light.

title: Shinagawa: Sunrise (Shinagawa, hinode)
note: A daimyo's retinue departs from the inns of Shinagawa at sunrise, with the bay and moored boats visible beyond the rooftops.

title: Kawasaki: The Rokugo Ferry (Kawasaki, Rokugo watashibune)
note: Travelers and horses wait to board flat-bottomed ferries crossing the Tama River (Rokugo) at Kawasaki, with Mount Fuji faint in the distance.
alt: Kawasaki, The Rokugo Ferry: travelers and horses wait to board ferries

title: Kanagawa: View of the Embankment (Kanagawa, dai no kei)
note: Teahouse touts pull at passing travelers along a steep embankment lined with waterside inns overlooking Kanagawa Bay.
alt: Kanagawa, View of the Embankment: teahouse touts pull at passing travelers

title: Hodogaya: Shinmachi Bridge (Hodogaya, Shinmachibashi)
note: A pack-horse train crosses the Shinmachi Bridge outside Hodogaya beneath windswept pines.
alt: Hodogaya, Shinmachi Bridge: a pack-horse train crosses the bridge beneath windswept pines

title: Totsuka: The Fork at Motomachi (Totsuka, Motomachi betsudo)
note: A traveler dismounts at a horse-changing station where the road forks at Motomachi, near Totsuka.
alt: Totsuka, The Fork at Motomachi: a traveler dismounts where the road forks

title: Fujisawa: Yugyo Temple (Fujisawa, Yugyoji)
note: Pilgrims and travelers cross a bridge into Fujisawa beneath the gate of Yugyōji, the town's namesake temple, seen on the hill above.

title: Hiratsuka: Nawate Road (Hiratsuka, Nawate michi)
note: Two travelers hurry along the straight embankment road (nawate) into Hiratsuka with Mount Ōyama rising behind them.
alt: Hiratsuka, Nawate Road: two travelers hurry along a straight embankment road

title: Oiso: Tora's Rain (Oiso, Tora ga ame)
note: Travelers are caught in a sudden shower on the shore road at Ōiso, a rain traditionally called "Tora ga ame" after the legendary courtesan Tora.

title: Odawara: The Sakawa River (Odawara, Sakawagawa)
note: Porters carry a palanquin and baggage across the shallow Sakawa River on the approach to Odawara Castle, visible on the far bank.
alt: Odawara, The Sakawa River: porters carry a palanquin and baggage across the river

title: Hakone: View of the Lake (Hakone, kosui no zu)
note: A daimyo procession winds along a jagged mountain trail above Lake Ashi, with the peaks of the Hakone range towering over the water.
look: The tiny procession winding down the zigzag path. The rock walls are tilted far steeper than any real mountain, and the lake lies quiet below them.

title: Mishima: Morning Mist (Mishima, asagiri)
note: Travelers and a packhorse emerge from thick morning fog near the torii gate of Mishima Taisha, Mount Fuji hidden entirely from view.
look: The mist is a smooth fade of colour, and the shrine gate and travellers come out of it; Fuji is somewhere behind.

title: Numazu: Twilight (Numazu, tasogare zu)
note: A pilgrim in a tengu mask and a pack-laden traveler walk along the Kano River at dusk beneath a full moon, geese overhead.
look: The traveller with a tengu mask on his back, the full moon, and the geese crossing the sky.
alt: Numazu, Twilight: a pilgrim in a tengu mask and a traveler with a pack

title: Hara: Mount Fuji in the Morning (Hara, asa no Fuji)
note: Two travelers cross a marshy plain at Hara beneath an enormous Mount Fuji filling the sky.
look: Fuji is drawn taller than any real view would show, over two small travellers on the marsh.

title: Yoshiwara: Mount Fuji on the Left (Yoshiwara, hidari Fuji)
note: Riders and porters follow a bend in the road at Yoshiwara from which Mount Fuji unusually appears on the left side of the frame.
alt: Yoshiwara, Mount Fuji on the Left: riders and porters follow a bend in the road

title: Kanbara: Evening Snow (Kanbara, yoru no yuki)
note: Three muffled figures trudge through a silent, heavy snowfall in Kanbara, a scene of snow the town rarely saw.
look: The snow is mostly bare paper, and three figures in hats and capes lean into it.
alt: Kanbara, Evening Snow: three muffled figures trudge through heavy snowfall

title: Yui: Satta Peak (Yui, Satta mine)
note: Travelers pause on the cliffside Satta Pass trail overlooking Suruga Bay, with Mount Fuji visible across the water.

title: Okitsu: The Okitsu River (Okitsu, Okitsugawa)
note: Porters ford the shallow Okitsu River carrying a mounted traveler and baggage toward the town.

title: Ejiri: Distant View of Miho (Ejiri, Miho enbo)
note: Boats sail Suruga Bay off Ejiri as the pine-covered spit of Miho stretches into the distance beneath Mount Fuji.
alt: Ejiri, Distant View of Miho: boats sail Suruga Bay off Ejiri

title: Fuchu: The Abe River (Fuchu, Abekawa)
note: Porters carry passengers and palanquins on their shoulders across the wide, shallow Abe River outside Fuchū.
look: Count the ways of crossing: some travellers are carried on shoulders, some in a palanquin.
alt: Fuchū, The Abe River: porters carry passengers and palanquins across the river

title: Mariko: Famous Tea Shop (Mariko, meibutsu chamise)
note: Travelers stop at a thatched roadside teahouse in Mariko famous for its grated-yam (tororo) soup, served by a woman with a child.
alt: Mariko, Famous Tea Shop: travelers stop at a thatched roadside teahouse

title: Okabe: Utsu Mountain (Okabe, Utsu no yama)
note: A line of travelers threads a narrow, tree-shaded mountain path over the Utsu Pass near Okabe.
alt: Okabe, Utsu Mountain: a line of travelers on a tree-shaded mountain path

title: Fujieda: Changing Porters and Horses (Fujieda, jinba tsugitate)
note: Porters and packhorses are exchanged at the station entrance to Fujieda as a new relay team takes over the baggage.
alt: Fujieda, Changing Porters and Horses: porters and packhorses exchanged at the station entrance

title: Shimada: The Suruga Bank of the Oi River (Shimada, Oigawa Sungan)
note: Porters and mounted travelers gather on the Suruga-side bank of the Ōi River at Shimada, waiting to be carried across since no bridge was permitted.
alt: Shimada, The Suruga Bank of the Oi River: porters and travelers gather on the bank

title: Kanaya: The Far Bank of the Oi River (Kanaya, Oigawa engan)
note: Palanquin bearers wade the Ōi River toward Kanaya on the river's far bank, mountains rising beyond.

title: Nissaka: Sayo Mountain Pass (Nissaka, Sayo no nakayama)
note: A traveler rests beside a huge roadside boulder on the steep Sayo-no-Nakayama pass above Nissaka.

title: Kakegawa: Distant View of Mount Akiba (Kakegawa, Akibasan enbo)
note: A kite flies over a river crossing near Kakegawa with the sacred peak of Mount Akiba visible on the horizon.

title: Fukuroi: Tea Stall (Fukuroi, dejaya no zu)
note: Travelers rest at an open-air tea stall on the plain outside Fukuroi, one of the smaller stations on the route.

title: Mitsuke: View of the Tenryu River (Mitsuke, Tenryugawa zu)
note: Ferrymen pole passengers across the broad Tenryū River near Mitsuke, with sandbars and distant hills beyond.

title: Hamamatsu: Winter Scene (Hamamatsu, fuyugare no zu)
note: Travelers warm themselves at a bonfire beneath a huge bare tree on the outskirts of Hamamatsu, Mount Fuji faint in the distance.
look: The bonfire under the huge bare tree, and the travellers warming themselves.

title: Maisaka: View of Imagiri (Maisaka, Imagiri shinkei)
note: Sailboats cross the calm waters of Lake Hamana at the Imagiri crossing near Maisaka, with Mount Fuji on the horizon.

title: Arai: View of Ferryboats (Arai, watashibune no zu)
note: A daimyo's ferry approaches the shore at the Arai checkpoint, one of the Tōkaidō's most heavily guarded barrier stations.

title: Shirasuka: View of Shiomi Slope (Shirasuka, Shiomizaka zu)
note: Travelers pause on the Shiomizaka hillside above Shirasuka, where the road briefly opens onto a view of the sea.

title: Futakawa: Sarugababa Plateau (Futakawa, Sarugababa)
note: A modest teahouse stands alone on the windswept Sarugababa plateau outside Futagawa as a samurai procession passes.

title: Yoshida: The Toyo River Bridge (Yoshida, Toyokawabashi)
note: Workers repair the long wooden bridge over the Toyo River at Yoshida beneath the walls of Yoshida Castle.
alt: Yoshida, The Toyo River Bridge: workers repair the long wooden bridge

title: Goyu: Women Stopping Travelers (Goyu, tabibito tomeru onna)
note: Innkeepers' women physically pull passing travelers by the sleeve into competing lodging houses at Goyu.
look: Watch the hands: the innkeepers' women are pulling travellers in by the sleeve.

title: Akasaka: Waitresses at an Inn (Akasaka, ryosha shofu no zu)
note: Serving women prepare an evening meal and entertain guests in the courtyard of an inn at Akasaka.

title: Fujikawa: View of Post Outskirts (Fujikawa, bohana no zu)
note: A small daimyo procession passes a solitary teahouse at the edge of Fujikawa as evening approaches.

title: Okazaki: Yahagi Bridge (Okazaki, Yahagi no hashi)
note: A daimyo procession crosses the immense Yahagi Bridge into Okazaki beneath its castle, one of the longest bridges on the Tōkaidō.

title: Chiryu: Early Summer Horse Market (Chiryu, shuka uma ichi)
note: Horses are bought and sold in an open field outside Chiryū during the town's famous early-summer horse market.

title: Narumi: Famous Tie-dyed Fabrics of Arimatsu (Narumi, meibutsu Arimatsu shibori)
note: Shops in Narumi display bolts of the tie-dyed cotton (Arimatsu shibori) for which the town was famous, as travelers browse.
alt: Narumi, Famous Tie-dyed Fabrics of Arimatsu: shops display bolts of tie-dyed cotton

title: Miya: Religious Festival at Atsuta Shrine (Miya, Atsuta shinji)
note: Wrestlers perform sumo before a crowd during a festival at Atsuta Shrine, the landmark of the port town of Miya.
alt: Miya, Religious Festival at Atsuta Shrine: wrestlers perform sumo before a crowd

title: Kuwana: The Landing of the Shichiri Ferry Crossing (Kuwana, Shichiri watashiguchi)
note: Sailboats approach the pier at Kuwana after the seven-ri sea crossing from Miya, since no direct road linked the two towns.
look: Sailboats and a pier: the sea crossing from Miya ends here.

title: Yokkaichi: Mie River (Yokkaichi, Miegawa)
note: A traveler's straw hat blows away in the wind as he crosses a plank bridge over the Mie River outside Yokkaichi.

title: Ishiyakushi: Ishiyakushi Temple (Ishiyakushi, Ishiyakushiji)
note: A quiet view of Ishiyakushi Temple and its surrounding pines is seen from the road, with little traffic on this small station.
alt: Ishiyakushi, Ishiyakushi Temple: the temple among its surrounding pines

title: Shono: Driving Rain (Shono hakuu)
note: Travelers and porters are caught in a sudden, driving rainstorm as they hurry along the road at Shōno.
look: The rain is drawn as slanting lines, and the bamboo and the hurrying travellers bend with it.
alt: Shōno, Driving Rain: travelers and porters hurry through a driving rainstorm

title: Kameyama: Weather Clearing after Snow (Kameyama, yukibare)
note: A procession climbs a steep, snow-covered slope toward Kameyama Castle as the sky clears after a snowfall.
look: The procession climbing toward the castle while the sky clears behind the snow.
alt: Kameyama, Weather Clearing after Snow: a procession climbs a snowy slope

title: Seki: Early Departure from the Main Camp (Seki, honjin hayadachi)
note: Porters and a palanquin assemble in the pre-dawn dark outside the honjin (main inn) at Seki as a party prepares to depart.
alt: Seki, Early Departure from the Main Camp: porters and a palanquin assemble before dawn

title: Sakanoshita: Peak of Fudesute Mountain (Sakanoshita, Fudesute mine)
note: Travelers pause at a teahouse overlooking a dramatic gorge and waterfall near the peak of Fudesute-yama.

title: Tsuchiyama: Spring Shower (Tsuchiyama, haru no ame)
note: Travelers cross a bridge over a swollen mountain stream at Tsuchiyama in a sudden spring downpour.

title: Minakuchi: Dried Gourd Shavings, A Local Specialty (Minakuchi, meibutsu kanpyo)
note: Women prepare and dry kanpyō (gourd shavings), the local specialty of Minakuchi, on racks outside a farmhouse.
alt: Minakuchi, Dried Gourd Shavings, A Local Specialty: women dry kanpyō

title: Ishibe: Megawa Village (Ishibe, Megawa no sato)
note: Travelers pass through the small hamlet of Megawa near Ishibe as the sun rises over distant hills.

title: Kusatsu: Famous Post House (Kusatsu, Meibutsu tateba)
note: Palanquin bearers and travelers crowd a large post-house courtyard at Kusatsu, where the Tōkaidō met the Nakasendō.

title: Otsu: Hashirii Teahouse (Otsu, Hashirii chaya)
note: Ox-carts loaded with goods pass a well-known teahouse at the edge of Ōtsu on the final approach to Kyoto.
alt: Ōtsu, Hashirii Teahouse: ox-carts loaded with goods pass a teahouse

title: Kyoto: The Great Bridge at Sanjo (Keishi, Sanjo ohashi)
note: Travelers and ox-carts cross the Sanjō Ōhashi bridge into Kyoto, with the city and hills beyond marking the end of the Tōkaidō.
look: The Sanjō Ōhashi bridge, ox-carts crossing, the hills of Kyoto behind. This is the end of the road.
alt: Kyoto, The Great Bridge at Sanjo: travelers and ox-carts cross the bridge into Kyoto
